cards.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, is wrapping up a letter to God's chosen people living as exiles (1 Peter 1:1). He's just told them not to be surprised by the fiery trial they're going through (1 Peter 4:12). Now he has a word for one group in the church: the elders.

cards.question: Peter is appealing to the church elders. True or false: he talks to them from a step above them, not as one of them.

cards.text: Peter calls himself a fellow elder, a witness of Christ's sufferings, and a partaker of the glory to be revealed. Then he gives the elders their job, and he paints it as a picture.

cards.question: What picture does Peter give the elders for their job with God's people?

cards.text: Then Peter tells them HOW: not out of compulsion, but willingly, as God would have you. In other words, NOT like a man dragging himself out of bed on his FIFTH snooze.

cards.question: Peter says the elders shouldn't shepherd God's flock out of greed. What should drive them instead?
Peter tells the elders not to lord it over the people entrusted to them. What should they be instead?

cards.text: And here's the payoff, friend. Peter says when the Chief Shepherd appears, the elders will receive the crown of glory.

cards.question: True or false: Peter says the crown of glory the elders receive will fade away one day.

cards.text: A crown that NEVER fades, and I can't keep a cookie from going stale past Tuesday. Next, Peter has a word for the young men.

cards.question: Peter turns to the young men in the church. What does he tell them to do toward their elders?

cards.text: Then Peter talks to ALL of them: clothe yourselves with humility toward one another. Put it on like I put on this apron, friend: every morning, no exceptions, no skipping days.

cards.question: Peter backs up his call to humility with a quote: God ___ the proud, but gives ___ to the humble.

cards.text: So, Peter says, humble yourselves under God's mighty hand, so that in due time He may exalt you. DUE time, friend, and I have opened enough ovens too early to respect those two words.

cards.question: Peter tells them to cast all their anxiety on God. What reason does he give?

cards.text: ALL of it, friend, even that bill sitting unopened on the counter for a week. Then Peter warns them to be sober-minded and alert, and he names their adversary: the devil.

cards.question: Peter warns that their adversary the devil prowls around looking for someone to devour. What does Peter say the devil is like?

cards.text: A roaring lion, seeking someone to devour. Friend, I'm a cookie stamper who JUMPS when the oven timer dings, so this verse has my full attention.

cards.question: True or false: Peter tells them to run from the devil instead of resisting him.
As they resist the devil and stand firm in their faith, what does Peter want them to know about their brothers throughout the world?

answers.text: They face the same kinds of suffering
They are praying for them every day
They have already won the fight

cards.text: So they're not alone in it. Then Peter looks past the suffering: after a little while, the God of all grace, who called them to His eternal glory in Christ, will step in Himself.

cards.question: After they have suffered for a little while, what does Peter say the God of all grace will do?

cards.text: Peter breaks into praise: "To Him be the power forever and ever. Amen." Then he says he wrote this letter through Silvanus, whom he calls a faithful brother.

cards.question: Peter sums up why he wrote: to encourage them and testify that this is the true ___ of God.

cards.text: Stand firm in it, Peter tells them. Then come the greetings, from the church in Babylon and from someone Peter calls his son.

cards.question: Peter passes along greetings from someone he calls "my son." Who is it?
True or false: as he closes, Peter tells them to greet one another with a kiss of love.

cards.text: And Peter signs off: "Peace to all of you who are in Christ." Friend, I've sealed a LOT of cookie boxes, and not one of them closed that sweet.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Guards for the flock" is close to true in the passage. In 1 Peter 5:2, Peter tells the elders to be shepherds "watching over them," and guarding the flock means much the same thing. A baker could argue this answer is right.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: "Guards for the flock" is a near-match to the elders' shepherding job described in 1 Peter 5:2.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The Chief Shepherd appears here for the first time, but the card never says simply who He is. The baker isn't told that this means Jesus, though the text clearly implies it.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This fill in the blank shows the quoted line word for word and asks the baker to fill in its missing words ("opposes," "grace"). The baker hasn't seen this wording, and nothing earlier lets them reason from grace over riches. It works like the Psalm 23 "He guides me in the paths of…" example of a bad card.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Because it will all pass" is arguably true within the passage. 1 Peter 5:10 says they will suffer only "for a little while" before God restores them, so a baker could argue that this answer is supported.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.
